course_name_original: Aplicaciones y Tratamiento de Datos en Tecnología y Física
course_name_en: Applications and Data Processing in Technology and Physics

learning_outcomes.text: Construction of machine learning systems using basic and advanced techniques to build intelligent systems from data sets.
Utilize advanced methods based on multivariate techniques for the analysis of complex data in Technology and Physics.
Know and use computational techniques and tools for data analysis in Technology and Physics.
Be able to define the most suitable strategy for the analysis of data from a complex physical or technological experiment.
Know the main current applications of data processing in physical technologies.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1. Artificial intelligence techniques in space-time modeling in materials physics.
Hamiltonian formalism for the description of a material in a space-time cylinder.
Variational methods to study the propagation of elastic waves in the medium, visco-elasticity, and damage models.
Topic 2. Tools and applications for atmospheric and space data analysis.
Advanced techniques for atmospheric data analysis: introduction to standard methods.
Description of ocean-climate system modeling algorithms based on convolutional neural networks, graph networks, Bayesian regression, and genetic programming.
Topic 3. Strategies for analyzing data streams from large facilities: example of Big Data at CERN's LHC.
Data analysis and processing flow of the LHC, focusing on dimensional data reduction techniques.
Automated learning techniques used in state-of-the-art data processing at each stage of the process, including anomaly detection with autoencoders and particle registration with graph networks.
Differentiable programming paradigm, optimization of data analysis flows, and the concept of inductive bias and its use in particle physics.
State-of-the-art examples in muonic and neutronic tomography, and equivariant neural networks.
Advanced computing: key elements of advanced computing systems in modern physics (CPUs, GPUs), recent advances in fast inference with FPGA, ASIC, neuromorphic chips, and quantum computing.
Infrastructure side: typical structure of a computing center, international computing network projects (GRID, EXASCALE), and commercial solutions (cloud computing on-demand).

assessment_methods.method: Attendance / Participation in Seminars and Tutorials (including online)
Active Participation in Forums and Virtual Campus Activities

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 0.1 * A + 0.1 * P + 0.55 * I + 0.25 * X, where A, P, I, and X are grades for Attendance, Participation, Reports, and Final Exam, all out of ten points. A minimum score of 3/10 is required on the final exam (X) to pass the course. If X < 3, the final score will be the minimum of the calculated score and 4.5. For extraordinary calls or part-time students, alternative evaluation involves a theoretical-practical exam (60%) and an individual project (40%), with a minimum of 3/10 on the exam.
